input.question: Just how different are the male and female brain?
input.ground_truth: There was a [thread](_URL_0_) earlier today in /r/AskScienceDiscussion about the brains of transgender men and women. You should give it a look, it has some interesting results about gender and brain morphology. It turns out the brains of transgender men and women most closely resemble the brains of the gender they identify with, not the sex they were born with. It also has some links to some of the primary literature about the sex differences in brain morphology. Should give you a good idea about how different the brains of men and women are.

Okay, let’s imagine the brains of boys and girls are like two different kinds of toy boxes.

Both toy boxes can hold lots of toys, and both have similar kinds of toys inside. But sometimes, the way the toys are arranged or which toys are inside a little bit more often can be a tiny bit different.

For example, some studies say that on average, boys’ brains might have a bit more of one kind of toy (like a truck), and girls’ brains might have a bit more of another kind (like a doll). But both boxes have lots of cars, dolls, blocks, and all sorts of fun things!

Also, every toy box is a little different, even if they are from the same boy or girl. So, while there are some small differences on average between boy and girl brains, they are still mostly the same, and every brain is special and unique!
